title: The Primogen
summary: Clan elders who sit on a Camarilla city's council.

claims.text: Unlike justicars, archons, sheriffs or scourges, primogen have few fixed duties beyond speaking for their clans, a duty read in many ways.
A primogen keeps the office as long as the right Kindred are content, or the discontented lack the power to act.
The primogen leads the clan politically, represents it on the council, advises it, marshals it in battle and punishes its lightest offences.
All real power a primogen holds comes from the clan, so keeping the clan satisfied matters most.

title: Origin of the Councils
summary: How elder councils arose during the Long Night.

claims.text: When elder coteries took a region together, they could split it, pick one of them as prince, or share rule as a council.
Split domains were often too small to defend and reunited, and choosing one ruler rarely happened without bloodshed.
Shared rule proved workable, to the surprise of the elders themselves.

title: Whip and Steward
summary: The assistants who serve a primogen.

claims.text: The whip keeps a primogen informed on clan matters, tries to keep council meetings moving, and runs errands.
In large cities a steward keeps the council chambers, tracks the primogen's schedule and decides who may see them; often the whip does both jobs.

title: Elder Salons
summary: Contests elders stage to fight boredom.

claims.text: Elders always look for challenges that do not risk their own unlives.
Scavenger hunt salons, where elders gather and race to find rare objects, alone, in teams or through agents, are not unusual.

title: Frank Hiltz
summary: The lone Malkavian of Jackson Hole, Wyoming.

claims.text: No other Malkavian lives in Jackson Hole, so Frank Hiltz holds the clan seat on its primogen council alone.
Holding no power beyond a single vote, Frank Hiltz has never been acknowledged by clan elders.

title: Primogen and Influence
summary: How primogen gain mortal influence through their clans.

claims.text: A primogen who takes influence from an underling is thought pitiful and is ruined socially if the harpies learn of it.
Trading contacts and influence with clanmates is accepted and can help both sides.
Ideal mortal contacts keep late hours, are easy to reach, live alone and have a secret to hide.

title: Unattached Councils
summary: Rare councils whose members do not represent clans.

claims.text: Members of an unattached council sit for knowledge or influence rather than as clan voices.
The city's Kindred have little say, a formal vote is unheard of, and the prince usually chooses alone.
